one_line: Zero-knowledge webmail with browser-side decryption and client-side WebMCP agent access.
what_it_does: Stores account and mail data as ciphertext on a relay while the browser decrypts it, and exposes mailbox actions to an agent through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: The submission makes a strong case that server-side MCP cannot operate on mail whose keys and plaintext remain in the browser; WebMCP shares the unlocked live mailbox state with the agent.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes six WebMCP tools registered directly with the page.
Transcript demonstrates inbox summarization and drafting a reply through ChatGPT.
Architecture claim is browser decryption with a ciphertext-only relay.
execution_rationale: Video transcript and frame sheets show a coherent zero-knowledge mail architecture, settings/developer states, and an end-to-end agent workflow, though the visual evidence is small and security claims are not independently verified.
execution_evidence: 159-second demo transcript covers decrypting saved account data, inbox summary, suspicious-message flagging, and reply drafting.
Frame sheet shows ciphertext, settings, browser inspection, and mail-server flow diagrams.
Devpost packaging identifies a dedicated WebMCP demo.
impact_rationale: Custom-domain and privacy-conscious email users have a concrete need for a modern private mailbox that remains agent-usable without surrendering plaintext to a service backend.
impact_evidence: Project describes daily-driver use for custom-domain email.
Transcript demonstrates practical inbox triage and reply drafting.
Zero-knowledge positioning directly addresses server visibility concerns.
creativity_rationale: Combining client-side zero-knowledge webmail with browser-native agent tooling is a memorable and technically ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Client-only agent access is positioned as the solution to the privacy architecture constraint.
Relay tunnels encrypted traffic while TLS terminates at browser and mail server endpoints.
usability_note: The demonstrated agent flows appear straightforward; mailbox setup and cryptographic UX are not fully visible.
red_flags: Cryptographic and zero-knowledge properties are claims rather than independently verified evidence.
standouts: Strong WebMCP indispensability argument grounded in client-side secrecy.
Shows useful mailbox operations rather than only tool registration.
advance_reason: High leverage with credible end-to-end agent evidence and a distinctive privacy architecture.

one_line: Learns web-form workflows, turns them into reusable WebMCP tools, and repairs them when pages change.
what_it_does: Captures a form flow, registers a named tool, detects drift, auto-repairs safe changes, and asks a human for missing information before submission.
leverage_rationale: The learned workflow becoming a callable structured tool, with persistent state and repair, is substantially more reliable than repeatedly driving arbitrary form UI.
leverage_evidence: About text says clinic_booking is created and discovered without reload.
Four page changes are compared; three repaired automatically and one escalated.
Human approval is required before consequential submission.
execution_rationale: The packet gives a detailed coherent central workflow and multiple gallery images, but has no video and the end-to-end behavior is claimed rather than observed.
execution_evidence: Description specifies learning, registration, drift detection, repair, approval, audit, and caching.
Gallery/frame references provide packaging imagery but no submitted video.
W3C survey cached-result behavior is explicitly described.
impact_rationale: Reusable resilient form automation addresses repetitive tasks for agents and people, especially where page redesigns otherwise break automations and human approval matters.
impact_evidence: Clinic booking is a concrete recurring workflow.
Repair escalation preserves a person’s ability to answer page-specific required fields.
Audit and accessibility checks broaden practical value.
creativity_rationale: Learning a task from the live form and maintaining it across UI drift is a fresh synthesis of browser automation, WebMCP, and human-in-the-loop repair.
creativity_evidence: Saved steps are callable tools rather than passive instructions.
Repair distinguishes deterministic page changes from information only a human can supply.
usability_note: Approval and repair escalation are well-considered; freshness/cached-page semantics may need careful user communication.
red_flags: No video evidence; runtime claims rely on text and images.
standouts: Concrete handling of changed required fields.
advance_reason: Strong, differentiated WebMCP workflow with credible practical impact despite unobserved execution.

one_line: Runtime for recovering unfinished workflows one verified step at a time.
what_it_does: Preserves intent, progress, failure evidence, capabilities, policies, and invariants so an agent can replan safely after workflow interruption.
leverage_rationale: Structured recovery state and deterministic verification offer a meaningful reliability improvement over an agent blindly replaying UI actions.
leverage_evidence: Pitch centers on unfinished-workflow recovery.
Description lists preserved intent, succeeded steps, failed route, policies, and invariants.
Every action is verified by deterministic application code.
execution_rationale: The concept and safety boundary are coherent, but the packet supplies no video and only limited concrete demo detail, so end-to-end completeness is uncertain.
execution_evidence: About text describes inspect, choose, sequence, observe, and replan loop.
Deterministic verification and constrained authority are explicitly claimed.
No video submitted and no gallery images are listed.
impact_rationale: Developers and workflow-heavy applications can benefit from preserving user intent and safe recovery instead of abandoning partially completed tasks.
impact_evidence: Motivation identifies lost intent and partial progress as a recurring application gap.
Invoice-like unfinished actions are given as a concrete use case.
creativity_rationale: The focus on recoverability and verified replanning is a useful, relatively original agent interaction model beyond ordinary tool calling.
creativity_evidence: Separates developer-defined legal actions from agent-discovered sequencing.
Treats failure evidence and invariants as first-class workflow state.
usability_note: Safety model is promising, but the user-facing recovery experience is not shown.
red_flags: Very thin visual/runtime evidence; concrete central workflow is not demonstrated.
standouts: Preserves user intent rather than merely retrying failed UI actions.
advance_reason: Interesting architecture, but execution evidence is too thin for advancement against demonstrated projects.

one_line: Lets a player ask an agent to remix a live browser game and immediately play the result.
what_it_does: Provides a playable KAPLAYGROUND-based editor where an agent can inspect, edit, run, check, and return a modified game while the creator remains director and tester.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP makes natural-language edits to a live game/editor state convenient and repeatable, though a general coding agent could achieve similar outcomes with more friction.
leverage_evidence: Description says the assistant changes the character to Bobo and the creator plays the result.
Agent can understand the open project, edit it, run it, and return checks.
Editor remains usable manually without an agent.
execution_rationale: A real playable editor and remix loop are described coherently, but the packet has no video and limited gallery evidence.
execution_evidence: About text states a real demo flow and playable result.
Manual editing, browser saves, and portable export are included.
No video submitted.
impact_rationale: Beginners and creators can experiment with game changes without setting up a local development environment, preserving immediate play/testing feedback.
impact_evidence: Explicit audience is creators who want to start from a working game.
Play, edit, save, and export are supported.
creativity_rationale: The creator-director/player-tester loop is an engaging application of agents to game remixing rather than code generation alone.
creativity_evidence: Natural-language remix followed by immediate play is the core interaction.
Builds on an existing editor while adding an agent collaboration workflow.
usability_note: Immediate play and manual fallback support approachable experimentation.
red_flags: Built on pre-existing KAPLAY/KAPLAYGROUND foundation; challenge-period additions are asserted but not independently visible.
standouts: Playable feedback closes the remix loop.
advance_reason: Memorable creative workflow with credible user value and adequate claimed product scope.

one_line: Purpose-aware WebMCP evaluator that tests whether tools deliver real journey outcomes.
what_it_does: Runs declared contracts against live page tools, records schemas/timing and before-after evidence, scores coverage and hygiene, and recommends repairs.
leverage_rationale: Prism directly tests the structured agent surface and observable shared state; its product purpose depends on WebMCP-level discovery and invocation rather than generic UI inspection.
leverage_evidence: Description says browser companion discovers and executes selected live WebMCP tools.
Captures privacy-preserving before-and-after mutation evidence.
Prism exposes four page-side tools to an agent itself.
execution_rationale: The evaluation model is coherent and detailed, with clear outputs and repair loops, but no video means runtime completion remains claimed.
execution_evidence: Four dimensions and evidence-backed scorecards are specified.
Concrete weak-cart example includes read-back verification recommendation.
Gallery/frame references but no video.
impact_rationale: WebMCP developers and evaluators need more than registration checks; journey-level mutation proof can prevent unreliable agent integrations from shipping.
impact_evidence: Targets commerce, project operations, and content editor contracts.
Every score includes evidence and a retestable repair.
creativity_rationale: Purpose contracts plus observable mutation proof are a strong original framing for WebMCP quality evaluation.
creativity_evidence: Evaluates whether tools cover a job-to-be-done and preserve human approval boundaries.
The evaluator is itself agent-addressable through WebMCP.
usability_note: Evidence-backed diagnostics are useful, though contract setup may be technical.
red_flags: No video evidence; live runner behavior is not directly observed.
standouts: Tests visible state mutation, not just tool presence.
Self-hosted evaluation surface is conceptually strong.
advance_reason: High WebMCP relevance and meaningful evaluator concept; execution deserves follow-up observation.

one_line: Browser-based Tailwind page builder whose editor actions are exposed to WebMCP agents.
what_it_does: Lets users visually build responsive pages while ChatGPT understands editor capabilities and modifies the page without external MCP setup.

impact_evidence: Author identifies beginners and non-technical WordPress users as the target.

creativity_evidence: Simplifies an existing WordPress editor and adds page-side WebMCP access.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP brings agent assistance into the same visible scientific workflow state, allowing GUI interaction, intermediate inspection, and human decisions instead of opaque chat-only analysis.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP lets each traveler’s agent query structured place data and write context into shared trip state while preserving independent choices, a meaningful improvement over one agent scraping or mediating everyone.
leverage_evidence: Four WebMCP tools are reported in Chrome Tool Inspector.

execution_evidence: Description specifies Explore, shared room, and map surfaces.

Gallery/frame references exist but no submitted video.

impact_evidence: Targets Korea visitors and people seeking events/places outside routine.

standouts: Exploration beyond routine is built into the product loop.
